THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 09.01.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:1753 BAIL APPL. NO.10794 OF 2024  2  P.V.KUNHIKRISHNAN, J  --------------------------------
 B.A.No.10794 of 2024  -------------------------------
 Dated this the 09th day of January, 2025  ORDER
This Bail Application is filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
2. Petitioner is an accused in Crime No.228/2024 of Punalur Police Station.

The above case is registered against the petitioner alleging offences punishable under Sections 376, 376(1), 376(2)(f),
376(2)(1), 376(2)(n), 506, 354 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code and, Sections 21(1), 7, 8, 5p, 51, 5k,
6(1), 3(a), 4(2), 4(1) of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

entities.text: Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The prosecution case is that, victim is a mentally challenged minor girl, who ought to be cared by the accused was subjected to sexual assault and penetrative sexual assault.

It is alleged that, the accused approached the victim, who was lying down in a room, removed her clothes,
2025:KER:1753 BAIL APPL. NO.10794 OF 2024 pressed and kissed her private body parts and committed rape.
Hence, it is alleged that the accused committed the offence.
4. Heard counsel for the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor.
5. The counsel for the petitioner submitted that, the petitioner is also a mentally challenged person suffers from 40% intellectual disability.
Annexure A2 is produced to show that petitioner's disability.
It is submitted that the victim is now in the child home and not residing with the petitioner.

It is also submitted that, the learned Magistrate recorded the statement of the victim in which she has no case that , she committed penetrative sexual intercourse except, the fact that the petitioner touched the private part of the victim.
6. The Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
The Public Prosecutor submitted that, the allegations against the petitioner are serious.
7. It is true that the allegations against the 2025:KER:1753 BAIL APPL. NO.10794 OF 2024 petitioner are very serious.
But, the facts remains that, as evident by Annexure A2, the petitioner is also a person suffers from 40% intellectual disability.
Victim is also a girl with some intellectual disability.
Admittedly, the victim is not staying with the petitioner now.

This court perused the FIS given by the victim in which there is allegation that the petitioner committed penetrative sexual Kamal Raj A vs State Of Kerala on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89340430/
2 intercourse.

entities.text: Kamal Raj A vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But the statement is recorded by the learned Magistrate under Section 183 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
This Court perused the same.
In that statement, she has no case of penetrative sexual intercourse, except the allegation that petitioner touched the private parts of the body of the victim.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, and also considering the fact that the petitioner is also suffering from disability, I think the petitioner can be granted bail after imposing stringent conditions.
8. Moreover, it is a well accepted principle that the bail is the rule and the jail is the exception.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Chidambaram.

P v Directorate of 2025:KER:1753 BAIL APPL. NO.10794 OF 2024 Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870], after considering all the earlier judgments, observed that, the basic jurisprudence relating to bail remains the same inasmuch as the grant of bail is the rule and refusal is the exception so as to ensure that the accused has the opportunity of securing fair trial.

entities.text: P v Directorate of 2025:KER:1753 BAIL APPL. NO.10794 OF 2024 Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Recently the Apex Court in Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
considered the point in detail.

entities.text: Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant paragraph of the above judgment is extracted hereunder.
"12. We may note that personal liberty is an important aspect of our constitutional mandate.

The occasion to arrest an accused during investigation arises when custodial investigation becomes necessary or it is a heinous crime or where there is a possibility of influencing the witnesses or accused may abscond.
Merely because an arrest can be made because it is lawful does not mandate that arrest must be made.
A distinction must be made between the existence of the power to arrest and the justification for exercise of it.
(Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189: (1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 2025:KER:1753 BAIL APPL. NO.10794 OF 2024 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981))

entities.text: Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189: (1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 2025:KER:1753 BAIL APPL. NO.10794 OF 2024 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If arrest is made routine, it can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self-esteem of a person.

If the Investigating Officer has no reason to believe that the accused will abscond or disobey summons and has, in fact, throughout cooperated with the investigation we fail to appreciate why there should be a compulsion on the officer to arrest the accused."
10.

In Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961], the Apex Court observed that even if the allegation is one of grave economic offence, it is not a rule that bail should be denied in every case.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering the dictum laid down in the above decision and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Bail Application is allowed with the following directions:
1.
The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within two weeks from today and shall undergo interrogation.

2. After interrogation, if the Investigating Officer propose to arrest the petitioner, he shall be released on bail on executing a bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the arresting officer concerned.
3. The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer for interrogation as and when required.

The petitioner shall co-operate with the investigation and shall not, directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
4. Petitioner shall not leave India without permission of the jurisdictional Court.

Petitioner shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected,
of the commission of which he is suspected.
6. Needless to mention, it would be well within the powers of the investigating officer to investigate the matter and, if necessary, to effect recoveries on the information, if any, given by the petitioner even while the petitioner is on bail as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) and another [2020 (1) KHC 663].
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any of the above conditions are violated by the petitioner, the jurisdictional Court can cancel the bail in accordance to law, even though the bail is granted by this Court.
The prosecution and the victim are at liberty to approach the jurisdictional Court 2025:KER:1753 BAIL APPL. NO.10794 OF 2024 to cancel the bail, if any of the above conditions are violated.
